solutions.check: clues read from the FT's printable PDF (PDF has no vector grid), the grid backsolved from their numbering, the one grid that fits; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Hobo travelling round north requiring food badly

indicators.note: the travelling word goes round the other letters, holding them inside

parts.note: someone travelling is going

indicators.note: the letters of north and food are put together badly, out of order

explanation.surface: A tramp wandering round the north who badly needs something to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges NORTH and FOOD into ODFORNOTH, and 'round' puts GOING around that run. 'requiring' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A hobo is a vagrant idler, the sort of worthless layabout people dismiss with this phrase.

clue.text: Exact focus of manicurist?

explanation.surface: What exactly does a manicurist concentrate on?
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means precisely or exactly right; literally, a manicurist works upon the fingernail.

clue.text: Conservative partial to European trip

indicators.note: the Conservative letter is taken as part of, within, the European word

parts.note: a Dane is a European from Denmark

explanation.surface: A Tory politician who is keen on a European holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partial to' looks like 'fond of' but here signals the C going inside DANE.
explanation.definitionFit: To trip, as in 'trip the light fantastic', is to move lightly on your feet in a step.

clue.text: Unexpected run to depose government

explanation.surface: A surprise run of events leads to a coup against the government.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an overthrow is an extra run scored when a fielder's return throw goes past the stumps; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket fielder's wild throw allows a bonus run; as a verb it means to topple rulers from power.

clue.text: Root vegetables born, may I add?

parts.note: née, used before a maiden name, means born
PS, postscript, is how a letter writer adds an afterthought

explanation.surface: A gardener's note listing root crops, with an afterthought tacked on.
explanation.walkthrough: NEEPS is the Scottish word for turnips or swedes, eaten with haggis.
explanation.definitionFit: Neeps is the Scots term for turnips and swedes, which are root crops.

clue.text: Dealer and master criminal

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked, so the letters of and plus master are bent out of order

explanation.surface: A dealer who is also a mastermind of crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' looks like a noun paired with 'master' but is the anagram signal working on AND and MASTER together.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman is a shopkeeper or merchant, someone who trades goods.

clue.text: Particular phrase fool's amended, finally

indicators.note: the word for fool is amended at its finish, its last letter being changed

parts.note: a fool is an idiot; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: A turn of phrase a fool has corrected at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amended, finally' changes only the last letter of IDIOT, the T becoming M; nothing in the clue supplies the M except the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom is an expression peculiar to a language, a set phrase whose meaning is its own.

clue.text: Common man beneath knowledge

indicators.note: in a down clue the man's name sits beneath, below, the knowledge word

parts.note: gen is slang for information or knowledge
Eric is a man's name

explanation.surface: An ordinary fellow whose learning is beneath him.
explanation.definitionFit: Generic means general or shared by a whole group, not specific or branded.

clue.text: A talent to eat seconds nowhere to be seen

indicators.note: the talent word takes in, eats, the letter for seconds

parts.note: a bent is a natural talent or aptitude

explanation.surface: A gifted eater wolfs down second helpings and vanishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Absent means missing, not present, so not able to be seen anywhere.

clue.text: Don't get out stick

explanation.surface: Told not to leave, someone stays put with a stick.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, to bat on is to keep batting without being dismissed (got out).
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it means keep batting in cricket; a baton is a short rod, like a conductor's or relay runner's.

clue.text: Happiness about version of the Bible reaching height

indicators.note: the happiness word goes about, around, the Bible version

parts.note: elation is great happiness
EV is an abbreviation for English Version, of the Bible

explanation.surface: Joy surrounds a new translation of scripture as it reaches the heights.
explanation.definitionFit: An elevation is a height above sea level or an altitude.

clue.text: Advice from Adam after strenuous exercise? That's the toughest challenge

definitions.text: Advice from Adam after strenuous exercise?

explanation.surface: The first man's tip after a workout leads to the hardest test of all.
explanation.walkthrough: Read in two pieces, Adam might tell his partner 'Eve, rest!'; the mountain stands for any supreme challenge. 'That's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The world's highest mountain is used figuratively for the ultimate goal or hardest feat.

clue.text: Taxman's head inside bowler, one cooking?

indicators.note: the taxman's head goes inside the bowler word

parts.note: a seamer is a cricket bowler who makes the ball deviate off its seam

indicators.note: the head of the taxman is his first letter

explanation.surface: A tax inspector's head is under his bowler hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bowler' suggests a hat, but it is a cricket bowler, a SEAMER.
explanation.definitionFit: A steamer is a pan or appliance that cooks food with steam.

clue.text: Sketch — or jot

explanation.surface: Draw a quick outline, or scribble a note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jot' is the noun, a tiny amount, as in 'not a jot'.
explanation.definitionFit: To trace is to draw over or outline; a trace is a minute amount, a whit.

clue.text: Irrational figure introduced to extraordinary miracle that's verifiable by observation

indicators.note: the irrational figure is put into the reordered letters
the letters of miracle are made extraordinary, rearranged out of their order

parts.note: pi is the best known irrational number

explanation.surface: A mathematician brings an illogical number to an amazing wonder that can be tested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extraordinary' rearranges MIRACLE as EMRICAL, and 'introduced to' places PI after EM.
explanation.definitionFit: Empirical knowledge rests on experiment and experience rather than theory.

clue.text: Popular entertainment, the sound of the sirens?

explanation.surface: A pop show likened to the song of the mythical sirens.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth the sirens sang from rocks to lure sailors to shipwreck.
explanation.definitionFit: A pop genre with guitars and drums; read literally, it is singing heard from the reefs.

clue.text: Craft giving access to fish?

parts.note: the carp is a freshwater fish
entry means access, a way in

explanation.surface: A boat that lets you get at the fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' looks like a boat but means a skill; the order is ENTRY 'to' CARP read as CARP then ENTRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Carpentry, woodworking, is a skilled trade or handicraft.

clue.text: Orpheus out to rescue queen, a life-saver?

indicators.note: the jumbled letters hold the queen safe inside them
out here means wrong or disordered, so the letters of Orpheus are muddled

parts.note: queen gives ER

explanation.surface: Orpheus sets out to save a queen from the underworld, a true rescuer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges ORPHEUS as SUPEHEO; 'to rescue' places R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A comic-book hero with special powers spends their time saving people.

clue.text: Penny entering wood with a little hesitation shows determination

indicators.note: the penny goes into the wood word

parts.note: willow is a tree and its wood, used for cricket bats
er is a short pause of hesitation in speech

explanation.surface: Someone pushes a coin into some timber, hesitating slightly but resolute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shows' and 'with' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Willpower is the strength of mind to carry through a purpose, resolve.

clue.text: Do as a dog — or bird

explanation.surface: Behave like a happy hound, or name a small bird.
explanation.definitionFit: As two words it is what a pleased dog does; it is also a small bird that bobs its tail.

clue.text: Country friend from Tyneside?

parts.note: Tyneside is in north-east England, abbreviated NE
a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: A rural mate who hails from Newcastle.
explanation.walkthrough: Tyneside is the Newcastle area of north-east England; the clue's order is reversed in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepal is a Himalayan kingdom, now republic, between India and China.

clue.text: Machine turning right, producing bubbles

parts.note: a lathe is a machine for turning wood or metal

explanation.surface: A machine spins to the right and froths up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' looks like a reversal signal but is part of the lathe's description; 'producing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Lather is foam, a mass of small soap bubbles.

clue.text: Moment cut short by wind in stomach

parts.note: gas is wind in the gut

indicators.note: the moment word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: a trice is a moment, as in 'in a trice'

explanation.surface: A brief pang caused by wind in the belly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' drops the E from TRICE; 'by' means beside.
explanation.definitionFit: Gastric is the adjective for things relating to or located in the stomach.

clue.text: Bird like a peregrine falcon?

explanation.surface: A bird compared to a fast-diving raptor.
explanation.definitionFit: A swift is a fast-flying bird; the falcon is famous for being speedy.

clue.text: Breakfast item pet dispensed with, black morsel

indicators.note: the word pet is removed from the breakfast item

parts.note: a crumpet is a griddle cake eaten toasted at breakfast or tea
taken as written
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A pet does without a breakfast treat, leaving a burnt scrap.
explanation.walkthrough: A CRUMPET is a British spongy griddle cake served toasted.
explanation.definitionFit: A crumb is a tiny fragment of bread or a small piece of anything.

clue.text: Though outstanding result at first, it's only part of the work

definitions.text: it's only part of the work

indicators.note: the though word stands outside the letter, holding it

parts.note: except can mean though or but, as in 'it would be fine, except it is raining'

indicators.note: the first letter of result is taken

explanation.surface: A section that, however brilliant at the start, is only a fragment of the whole piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outstanding' looks like praise but means standing outside: EXCEPT goes round R.
explanation.definitionFit: An excerpt is a passage taken from a longer book, film or score.

clue.text: Pole up north has to live in vehicle

indicators.note: the live word goes in the vehicle

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
to be is to exist or live

explanation.surface: A northerner's pole has to be kept in the car.
explanation.walkthrough: A caber is the tree trunk tossed in Scottish Highland games, hence 'up north'. 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A caber is a long wooden pole thrown in Scottish athletics.

clue.text: Battle in which you might try a drink?

parts.note: gin is a drink
a court is where cases are tried

explanation.surface: A clash where you might sample a beverage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'try' looks like 'taste' but means try in law. AGINCOURT is the 1415 English victory in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Agincourt was a famous battle of 1415 won by Henry V over the French.

clue.text: Neighbouring characters in prefab revealed, note

indicators.note: adjacent letters inside the phrase prefab revealed are taken together

explanation.surface: Next-door letters in a prefab building exposed a musical note.
explanation.definitionFit: A breve is a long musical note, double the length of a semibreve.

clue.text: Toilet, or symbol used for toilet

explanation.surface: A loo, or the sign on a loo door.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, a figure of a small boy is the usual picture on a gents' door.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a coy euphemism for the gents; the door sign shows a little lad.
